\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خامی} (khāmī)}{خامی (khāmī)}]{\ur{خامی} (khāmī) — a shortcoming}

\label{lesson:UR-C455-khami}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a good quality, then the Urdu for a personality.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خامی}}
\textbf{\ur{خامی}} — \emph{khāmī} — \textquotedblleft{}a shortcoming\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہر} \ur{انسان} \ur{میں} \ur{کوئی} \ur{نہ} \ur{کوئی} \ur{خامی} \ur{ہوتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{har insān meṅ koī na koī khāmī hotī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone has some shortcoming or other.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خامی}} (\emph{khāmī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khāmī}, \textquotedblleft{}rawness\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{khām}, \textquotedblleft{}raw, unripe\textquotedblright{}: a shortcoming is something not yet ripe.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khāmī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khāmī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{har insān meṅ koī na koī khāmī hotī hai.} — Everyone has some shortcoming or other.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a good quality, then the Urdu for a personality, then say \emph{khāmī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{خامی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A shortcoming\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for a personality, then the Urdu for a shortcoming.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غافل} (ghāfil)}{غافل (ghāfil)}]{\ur{غافل} (ghāfil) — heedless; careless}

\label{lesson:UR-C455-ghafil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for headstrong, then the Urdu for slothful.

\textbf{\ur{غافل}} — \emph{ghāfil} — \textquotedblleft{}heedless; careless\textquotedblright{}.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Bored or Curious to Faults and Flaws}

\label{lesson:UR-R455-review-448-455}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for fed up and interesting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item fed up, interesting, curiosity, eager, to feel about for
  \item a mother's love, tender affection, to kiss, to cling tightly, passionate love
  \item lonely, on one's own, separation, to whimper, out of sight
  \item to hesitate, to blush, remorse, contrite, embarrassment
  \item arrogance, boasting, to put on airs, fussiness, haughtiness
  \item to make (someone) laugh, to make (someone) cry, a burst of laughter, to sob, teasing
  \item a person's nature, disposition, a habit, a good quality, a personality
  \item a shortcoming, a defect, headstrong, slothful, heedless
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Fed up? (\textbf{\ur{بیزار}}, \emph{bezār}.) Interesting? (\textbf{\ur{دلچسپ}}, \emph{dilchasp}.) Curiosity? (\textbf{\ur{تجسس}}, \emph{tajassus}.) Eager? (\textbf{\ur{بیتاب}}, \emph{betāb}.) To feel about for? (\textbf{\ur{ٹوہنا}}, \emph{ṭohnā}.) A mother's love? (\textbf{\ur{ممتا}}, \emph{mamtā}.) Tender affection? (\textbf{\ur{شفقت}}, \emph{shafqat}.) To kiss? (\textbf{\ur{چومنا}}, \emph{chūmnā}.) To cling tightly? (\textbf{\ur{چمٹنا}}, \emph{chimaṭnā}.) Passionate love? (\textbf{\ur{عشق}}, \emph{ishq}.) Lonely? (\textbf{\ur{تنہا}}, \emph{tanhā}.) On one's own? (\textbf{\ur{اکیلا}}, \emph{akelā}.) Separation? (\textbf{\ur{جدائی}}, \emph{judāī}.) To whimper? (\textbf{\ur{بسورنا}}, \emph{bisūrnā}.) Out of sight? (\textbf{\ur{اوجھل}}, \emph{ojhal}.) To hesitate? (\textbf{\ur{ہچکچانا}}, \emph{hichkichānā}.) To blush? (\textbf{\ur{لجانا}}, \emph{lajānā}.) Remorse? (\textbf{\ur{ندامت}}, \emph{nadāmat}.) Contrite? (\textbf{\ur{پشیمان}}, \emph{pashemān}.) Embarrassment? (\textbf{\ur{خجالت}}, \emph{khijālat}.) Arrogance? (\textbf{\ur{غرور}}, \emph{ghurūr}.) Boasting? (\textbf{\ur{شیخی}}, \emph{shekhī}.) To put on airs? (\textbf{\ur{اترانا}}, \emph{itrānā}.) Fussiness? (\textbf{\ur{نخرا}}, \emph{nakhrā}.) Haughtiness? (\textbf{\ur{تکبر}}, \emph{takabbur}.) To make (someone) laugh? (\textbf{\ur{ہنسانا}}, \emph{hãsānā}.) To make (someone) cry? (\textbf{\ur{رلانا}}, \emph{rulānā}.) A burst of laughter? (\textbf{\ur{قہقہہ}}, \emph{qahqahā}.) To sob? (\textbf{\ur{سسکنا}}, \emph{sisaknā}.) Teasing? (\textbf{\ur{مذاق}}, \emph{mazāq}.) A person's nature? (\textbf{\ur{فطرت}}, \emph{fitrat}.) Disposition? (\textbf{\ur{طبیعت}}, \emph{tabīat}.) A habit? (\textbf{\ur{عادت}}, \emph{ādat}.) A good quality? (\textbf{\ur{خوبی}}, \emph{khūbī}.) A personality? (\textbf{\ur{شخصیت}}, \emph{shakhsiyat}.) A shortcoming? (\textbf{\ur{خامی}}, \emph{khāmī}.) A defect? (\textbf{\ur{عیب}}, \emph{aib}.) Headstrong? (\textbf{\ur{خودسر}}, \emph{khudsar}.) Slothful? (\textbf{\ur{کاہل}}, \emph{kāhil}.) Heedless? (\textbf{\ur{غافل}}, \emph{ghāfil}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
